title: "RSV forecasting workflow"
format: pdf

# Goal

We want to test whether **fine-tuning InfluPaint on RSV** beats **training a
DDPM from scratch on RSV** ("RSVpaint"), and how much that depends on **how much
RSV data** the model sees. Both models treat an epidemic season as an image
(time x location) and use a diffusion model to generate plausible season
trajectories. Inpainting then conditions those generated images on the partial
season we have already observed, which gives us forecasts.

To do that fairly we:

1. Hold out the latest RSV season (2025-26) so no model sees it during training.
   This held-out slice is also what we send to @bestill3 (Yue) for evaluation.
2. Build training pools that vary **one thing at a time**: the amount of real
   surveillance data (100% / 50% / 25%), plus a synthetic-only and an
   all-data reference. Source ratios are kept consistent across the amounts.
3. Train two versions on the surveillance pools:
   * `scratch`  - fresh DDPM trained only on RSV ("RSVpaint").
   * `finetune` - pre-trained InfluPaint checkpoint, further trained on RSV.
4. Compare them on the held-out season.

---

# Training data at a glance

A **frame** is one season-image: 53 weeks x states for one
(source, season, trajectory). Surveillance sources give one frame per season;
the Scenario Modelling Hub gives many synthetic trajectories per season.

**All RSV data available** (`RSV_FILLED.parquet`):

| Source    | Kind                                        | Seasons present              | Frames |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------|------------------------------|-------:|
| NHSN      | surveillance - hosp. admissions, all 51 states | 2023, 2024, 2025          | 3      |
| NSSP      | surveillance - ED-visit proportion, all states | 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025    | 4      |
| RSV-Net   | surveillance - lab-confirmed hosp., ~14 states | 2018-2025 (8 seasons)     | 8      |
| RSV_SMH   | synthetic - Scenario Modelling Hub          | 2023 (1600), 2024 (1500), 2025 (700) | 3800 |

Totals: **15 surveillance frames + 3800 synthetic frames**. (Seasons are named
by start year: 2025 = the 2025-26 season.)

**After holding out the validation season** (fluseason 2025, all sources),
training sees:

| Source              | Training seasons   | Frames |
|---------------------|--------------------|-------:|
| NHSN                | 2023, 2024         | 2      |
| NSSP                | 2022, 2023, 2024   | 3      |
| RSV-Net             | 2018-2024          | 7      |
| **Surveillance**    |                    | **12** |
| RSV_SMH (synthetic) | 2023, 2024         | 3100   |

So the **real surveillance pool the experiment varies is exactly 12 frames**.

---

# The models we train

Eight models. Everything is held fixed (architecture `scn868`, 64x64 images,
batch size 512) except the training pool and the initialisation.

| Model              | Init     | Training pool                       | Unique frames | Samples | Epochs |
|--------------------|----------|-------------------------------------|--------------:|--------:|-------:|
| RSVpaint-100S      | scratch  | surveillance 100%                   | 12            | 2160    | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-50S       | scratch  | surveillance 50%                    | 6             | 1080    | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-25S       | scratch  | surveillance 25%                    | 3             | 540     | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-100M      | scratch  | synthetic only                      | 3100          | 3100    | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-100A      | scratch  | all data (30% surv + 70% synthetic) | mixed         | ~2160   | 3000   |
| InfluPaint-ft-100S | finetune | surveillance 100%                   | 12            | 2160    | 500    |
| InfluPaint-ft-50S  | finetune | surveillance 50%                    | 6             | 1080    | 500    |
| InfluPaint-ft-25S  | finetune | surveillance 25%                    | 3             | 540     | 500    |

For the surveillance ladder, samples = unique frames x180 (see below). Synthetic
frames are plentiful so `100M` is used as-is (no oversampling); `100A` mixes the
two to a fixed total by proportion.

**The surveillance ladder (100S / 50S / 25S).** This is the core experiment.
We take the 12 surveillance frames and keep 100%, 50%, 25% of them, holding the
source ratio as even as integers allow and never dropping a source (NHSN must
stay in - it is the signal we condition on and score against at inference). For
50S/25S we keep the **most-recent** seasons of each source (closest to the
held-out season):

| Mix  | NHSN | NSSP | RSV-Net | Frames | x180 |
|------|-----:|-----:|--------:|-------:|-----:|
| 100S | 2    | 3    | 7       | 12     | 2160 |
| 50S  | 1    | 2    | 3       | 6      | 1080 |
| 25S  | 1    | 1    | 1       | 3      | 540  |

Every frame is then replicated **x180**, so the pools are 2160 / 1080 / 540
samples - all above the 512 batch size. Because the multiplier (180) and the
epoch count (3000) are **identical** across the ladder, each frame gets exactly
the same exposure regardless of pool size. The **only** difference between
RSVpaint-100S and RSVpaint-50S is that half the unique surveillance frames are
missing in the latter. That is what makes "how much data" a clean variable.

(Replicated copies are not identical: the mixer fills each copy's missing states
with random real surveillance data, and training adds on-the-fly augmentation -
Poisson noise, time shifts - so the 180 copies of a season never look the same
to the model.)

**Reference pools.** `100M` = synthetic only (does synthetic data alone work?).
`100A` = all RSV data, balanced 30% surveillance + 70% synthetic (does adding
synthetic to surveillance help?).

**Init.** `scratch` = RSVpaint (random init). `finetune` = start from a trained
flu InfluPaint checkpoint and keep training on RSV. The finetune arms mirror the
surveillance ladder, so finetune-vs-scratch differs only in initialisation.
Finetune uses 500 epochs (not 3000) because it starts from already-trained
weights.

# Scripts

Every step below maps to one script in this `RSV/workflow/` folder. Run from the
repo root (`/Users/cy/.../influpaint/`).

| Step | Script | What it does |
|------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | `validation_split.R` | Drops the held-out season from the data; saves train + validation parquets. |
| 2 | `build_training_sets.py` | Builds one `.nc` training file per mix (100S, 50S, 25S, 100M, 100A). |
| 3 | `workflow.qmd` (this file) | Quick inspection plots. |
| 4 | `train_rsv.run` + `rsv_training.py` | SLURM submits one training job per model. |
| 5 | `rsv_inpaint.py` | Inpaints one checkpoint into a Hubverse forecast CSV (+ raw draws). |
| 6 | `plot_forecasts_validation.py` | State-level forecast-vs-truth figure, one per model. |

---

# Step 1 - Hold out the validation season

**In one sentence:** split `RSV_FILLED.parquet` into a training file (held-out
season removed) and a validation file (only the held-out season).

We hold out **fluseason 2025 (the 2025-26 season)**: train on the past, forecast
the most recent season. The split filters **all sources** (NSSP, RSV-Net, NHSN,
RSV_SMH) by season, so even synthetic trajectories for that year are excluded -
nothing leaks. Edit `VALIDATION_SEASONS` at the top of `validation_split.R` to
change it.

```{bash}
Rscript RSV/workflow/validation_split.R
```

This produces `RSV/data/RSV_TRAIN.parquet` (what the models may see) and
`RSV/data/RSV_VALIDATION.parquet` (what Yue gets for evaluation). The report it
prints should show 12 surveillance frames in training (NHSN 2, NSSP 3,
RSV-Net 7).

---

# Step 2 - Build the training datasets

**In one sentence:** turn `RSV_TRAIN.parquet` into one 4D tensor (saved as
`.nc`) per mix, ready for PyTorch.

Each `.nc` file is a stack of season-images. An image is a 64x64 grid where rows
are weeks (1-53, padded to 64) and columns are locations (padded to 64); a pixel
is an incidence value. The recipes live at the top of `build_training_sets.py`:

- `SURVEILLANCE_LADDER` - the 100S / 50S / 25S frame counts per source (see the
  ladder table above). Each surviving frame is replicated `MULTIPLIER` (=180)
  times.
- `REFERENCE_POOLS` - `100M` (synthetic only) and `100A` (30% surv + 70%
  synthetic).

The 50S/25S rungs are built by `select_recent_seasons`, which drops whole
seasons so a smaller rung is literally a larger rung with frames removed. The
multiplier never changes, so smaller pools do fewer gradient steps per epoch
(25S = 1 batch/epoch, 100S = 4) - an intended consequence of having less data,
not a difference in per-frame exposure.

```{bash}
PYTHONPATH=. python RSV/workflow/build_training_sets.py \
    --input RSV/data/RSV_TRAIN.parquet \
    --outdir training_datasets \
    --tag 2026-06-23
```

This writes `training_datasets/RSV_<mix>_2026-06-23.nc` for each mix. The
`--tag` is what the SLURM scripts look for, so remember it. To rebuild one mix
while iterating: `--only 100S`.

---

# Step 3 - Quick look at a built dataset

**In one sentence:** open one `.nc` file and sanity-check its contents.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from influpaint.utils import SeasonAxis, plotting as idplots

season_setup = SeasonAxis.for_flusight(remove_us=True, remove_territories=True)

# Edit this path to whichever mix you want to inspect
arr = xr.open_dataarray("training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc")

print("Shape (samples, features, weeks, places):", arr.shape)
print("Mix config used:", arr.attrs["mix_cfg"])
print("First 5 origins :", arr.attrs["main_origins"][:5])
```

Plot a few sample trajectories on the US state grid. These should look like
realistic RSV seasons -- a winter rise, a peak around week 20-30 of the season
(December-February), and a decline afterwards.

```{python}
fig, ax = idplots.plot_us_grid(
    data=arr,
    season_axis=season_setup,
    sample_idx=list(np.arange(0, 5 * 17, step=17)),
    multi_line=True,
    sharey=False,
)
```

If anything looks off (wrong axes, all zeros, wildly different scales) stop and
fix it before spending cluster time.

# Step 4 - Train on Longleaf

**In one sentence:** submit one SLURM job per model; each runs `rsv_training.py`
on one L40 GPU.

Two pieces:

- `rsv_training.py` is the Python entry point. Given a `.nc` file, a scenario ID
  (which picks the U-Net + DDPM shape), and optionally a pre-trained checkpoint,
  it trains one model and logs everything to MLflow.
- `train_rsv.run` is the SLURM script. Its `RUN_TABLE` lists the 8 models; each
  row is one SLURM array task.

**Important:** the scenario ID is fixed to `868` across all runs so the
architectures match. That is what makes the finetune step legal - you can only
load InfluPaint weights into a model with the same shape.

| Run tag        | Mix  | Mode     | Epochs |
|----------------|------|----------|-------:|
| `100S_scratch`  | 100S | scratch  | 3000 |
| `50S_scratch`   | 50S  | scratch  | 3000 |
| `25S_scratch`   | 25S  | scratch  | 3000 |
| `100M_scratch`  | 100M | scratch  | 3000 |
| `100A_scratch`  | 100A | scratch  | 3000 |
| `100S_finetune` | 100S | finetune | 500  |
| `50S_finetune`  | 50S  | finetune | 500  |
| `25S_finetune`  | 25S  | finetune | 500  |

All scratch runs use 3000 epochs (an earlier attempt at 300 for the small
surveillance mixes did not converge: 1-4 batches/epoch x 300 epochs is far too
few gradient steps). Finetune mode loads only the model weights from
`FLUPAINT_CKPT` (not the optimizer state - loading a foreign optimizer state
makes the loss blow up to the millions); a fresh optimizer is essential. This is
controlled by `weights_only=True` in `rsv_training.py`.

Before you submit, edit `train_rsv.run`:

- `DATE_TAG` must match what you used in step 2.
- `FLUPAINT_CKPT` must point to a readable InfluPaint checkpoint on Longleaf
  (same scenario ID as `SCN_ID`).
- `REPO_ROOT`, `PYTHON` must match your account on Longleaf (the script exports
  `PYTHONPATH=$REPO_ROOT` before running so the package imports).
- `EXPERIMENT_NAME` is the MLflow experiment; change it for a new round.

Ship the repo + built `.nc` files to Longleaf, then:

### Login to UNC Longleaf
1. Sign into CISCO AnyConnect VPN with your UNC credentials.
2. In the terminal login to LongLeaf with your UNC credentials:
```bash
ssh cgeisma1@longleaf.unc.edu
srun -p jlessler --gres=gpu:1 --mem=64G --time=10:00:00 --nodelist="g1803jles01" --pty /bin/zsh
```

3. Transfer NC files and the repo to Longleaf (from your local machine):
```bash
rsync -avz --progress \
  "/Users/cy/Documents/PROJECTS LOCAL/influpaint/training_datasets/RSV_"*"_2026-06-23.nc" \
  cgeisma1@longleaf.unc.edu:/proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint/training_datasets/
```
Check that the files are there:
```bash
ls training_datasets/RSV_*_2026-06-23.nc
```

4. Connect to remote via SSH in VSCode and run in the terminal:
```bash
cd /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint
sbatch RSV/workflow/train_rsv.run
# resubmit only specific tasks (e.g. after a failure):
# sbatch --array=1-7 RSV/workflow/train_rsv.run
```

### Monitor jobs

There are two log files per task:

- `slurm-<jobid>_<task>.out` — bash output (the `=== SLURM array task N ===`
  header). If a job fails before Python starts (e.g. wrong `cd`) the error
  is here.
- `out_rsv_<experiment>_<run_tag>.out` — Python stdout/stderr. Loss curves,
  tracebacks, the final `Done. Checkpoint: ...` line.

```bash
# Active jobs (PD = pending, R = running)
squeue -u cgeisma1

# History of a finished batch (success / fail / timeout)
sacct -u cgeisma1 -j <jobid> --format=JobID,JobName,State,ExitCode,Elapsed

# Watch a specific run's training output
tail -f out_rsv_rsv-2026-06-23_100S_scratch.out

# Cancel specific tasks (e.g. before they start)
scancel <jobid>_5 <jobid>_6 <jobid>_7

# Quick scan for completed runs
grep "Done. Checkpoint" out_rsv_rsv-2026-06-23_*.out
```

Each job saves its checkpoint under
`OUTDIR/<git_hash>_<experiment>_<date>/` (set `OUTDIR` in `train_rsv.run`).
MLflow keeps loss curves and generated sample plots for every run.

### Smoke test before the real submission

Before burning cluster time, do a 2-epoch dry run in an interactive GPU job to
confirm the dataset loads and the loss goes down.

First, make the package importable (only needed once per shell session):
```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint:$PYTHONPATH
```

Then run:
```bash
python RSV/workflow/rsv_training.py \
    --dataset-nc training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc \
    --scn-id 868 \
    --experiment-name rsv-smoketest \
    --run-tag smoketest \
    --epochs 2 \
    --batch-size 64 \
    --outdir /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/
```

If that succeeds (a `.pth` file appears and MLflow shows a curve), the full
SLURM submission is safe.

### After all runs finish

Each successful run writes its checkpoint to
`/proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/<git_hash>_<experiment>_<date>/`.
Because the git hash changes between submissions, the 8 final checkpoints
end up scattered across a few folders. Consolidate them into one place:

```bash
mkdir -p /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
cp /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/*/{scratch,finetune}_*_scn868_ep*.pth \
   /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
ls -lh /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
```

You should end up with 8 `.pth` files - the inputs to step 5.

### Inspect training quality

Two helper scripts read the per-run `out_rsv_*.out` and `samples_*.npy`
artifacts and write PNGs you can preview in VSCode:

```bash
# Loss curves for every run (log y-axis)
python RSV/workflow/plot_losses.py
# -> rsv_training_losses.png

# 12 sanity samples per run as 64x64 heatmaps
python RSV/workflow/plot_samples.py \
  /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/*/samples_*.npy
# -> one .png per .npy, next to it
```

# Step 5 - Inpaint the held-out season (forecasting)

**In one sentence:** take ONE trained checkpoint and fill in the unobserved
weeks of the held-out season, then write the result as a Hubverse CSV (exactly
the shape you would submit to the CDC RSV Forecast Hub).

How inpainting works here, in plain terms: the model learned to draw a whole RSV
season as a 64x64 image (rows = weeks, columns = states). We paint in the weeks
we have already observed, lock those pixels, and let the model fill in the rest
of the season. The filled-in part is the forecast. We draw `batch_size`
independent fills, so the spread across draws gives the forecast quantiles.

The script is `RSV/workflow/rsv_inpaint.py`. Two things make it RSV-specific
(this is why we do not just reuse the flu notebook as-is):

1. **Scaling must match training.** A diffusion model works on normalised
   numbers; to read its output back as real RSV values you must undo that
   normalisation with the *same* scaling used in training. That scaling comes
   from the training `.nc` file, so you pass the **same-mix** `.nc` the
   checkpoint was trained on (`finetune_100S_*.pth` -> `RSV_100S_<tag>.nc`).
   Passing a different mix's `.nc` silently rescales every forecast.
2. **Ground truth is the held-out parquet, not a flu hub.** It is built with
   `GroundTruth.from_rsv(...)` from one surveillance signal (default `NHSN`,
   hospital admission counts, which reports all states) for the held-out
   season (2025). Whatever signal you choose is used *both* as the weeks you
   condition on and as the weeks you score against, so the forecast comes out
   in that signal's units.

**Mask / horizon convention:** `--reference-date` is a Saturday. Weeks ending
*before* it are treated as known; horizon 0 is the reference week itself (the
first unobserved week), and the Hubverse horizons `0, 1, 2, 3` are emitted.
`target_end_date = reference_date + 7 x horizon`. The target is
`wk inc rsv hosp` (NHSN hospitalizations). We drop the hub's `-1` backcast: on
final held-out data it is just a week we already observed and locked into the
model, so it carries no forecast information.

**Why NHSN and not RSV-Net:** the ground-truth signal is used both to
condition on and to score against, so coverage matters. NHSN reports all 51
states, giving a complete conditioning image. RSV-Net reports only ~14
states, which would force the other ~37 to zero in the known weeks and lie to
the model about where RSV is. `NSSP` (target `wk inc rsv prop ed visits`) is
the other full-coverage option if you want ED-visit proportion instead of
hospitalizations.

### Smoke test (one checkpoint, one date)

On Longleaf, in an interactive GPU job, from the repo root:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
python RSV/workflow/rsv_inpaint.py \
    --checkpoint /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/finetune_100S_finetune_scn868_ep500.pth \
    --dataset-nc training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc \
    --reference-date 2025-12-20 \
    --signal NHSN \
    --season 2025 \
    --outdir RSV/forecasts_validation
```

This writes `RSV/forecasts_validation/2025-12-20-UNC_IDD-InfluPaint-RSV.csv`
and the raw draws (`2025-12-20_draws_ti.npy`). To eyeball forecast vs reality,
run the plotting step below: the median should track the observed curve up to
the reference date and fan out afterwards. If the scale looks wrong (forecasts
orders of magnitude off the observed line), the most likely cause is a
`--dataset-nc` that does not match the checkpoint's mix.

### Scaling up

Once the smoke test looks right, loop over the 8 checkpoints and a handful of
reference dates through the season (e.g. one per month), then hand the CSVs to
Yue for scoring against `RSV_VALIDATION.parquet`. On Longleaf this is the
`inpaint_rsv.run` array job (8 models x 18 reference weeks).

### Step 6 - Plot forecast vs truth

After the sweep, render one state-level summary figure per model:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
python RSV/workflow/plot_forecasts_validation.py
# -> RSV/forecasts_validation/<MODEL>/<MODEL>_forecast_validation.png  (one per model)
```

Each figure is two rows over four states (North Carolina, New York, Texas,
Florida). The **top row** shows the 4-week-ahead forecasts (Hubverse horizons
0..3) at several reference dates; the **bottom row** shows the full-season
forecasts with a few example trajectories. Black is the observed NHSN truth and
each reference date gets its own color (shared across both rows). The forecast
quantiles and trajectories come from the 512 conditional draws in each
`*_draws_ti.npy`; ground truth is rebuilt with `GroundTruth.from_rsv` on the
held-out NHSN parquet, so truth and forecast are aligned by construction.

Useful flags: `--model RSVpaint-100S` (one model only), `--states NC NY TX FL`,
`--n-refs 5` (reference dates shown), `--n-traj 10` (trajectories per date), and
`--xlim-start` / `--xlim-end` (season window).
